findings.title: Externally published marked text bypasses command handling
findings.message: Composition handling is gated on s->before rather than the presence of marked text. vellum_input_update can publish marked text without a baseline, so cancelOperation: forwards the key instead of reaching finish's explicit cancellation refusal. The same gating in keyDown: and command forwarding allows shortcuts to reach the original view while that externally published composition is still marked.
findings.suggestion: Use a shared composition predicate such as s->before != nil || s->marked.location != NSNotFound for Escape, cancelOperation:, and pre-forwarding completion. Let finish reject cancellation without a baseline and transactionally unmark before forwarding other commands.
findings.evidence:
if(selector==@selector(cancelOperation:) && s->before){if(finish(s,YES))[[self inputContext] discardMarkedText];return;}
 if(s->before){if(!finish(s,NO)){s->keyEvent=nil;return;}[[self inputContext] discardMarkedText];}forwardKey(self);

findings.title: External updates retain an obsolete cancellation snapshot
findings.message: An acknowledged publication can replace the text and selection while retaining marked text, but the saved cancellation baseline remains unchanged. If the application publishes an external edit during a native composition, Escape subsequently restores the older entire document from s->before, silently losing that accepted edit.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish an unchanged acknowledgement from a divergent external publication. For a divergent publication that retains marked text, rebase the cancellation snapshot using an explicitly supplied baseline, or clear the old baseline and explicitly refuse cancellation rather than restoring obsolete text.

findings.title: Deactivate native input when the field loses focus
findings.message: Native input activation uses the last registered widget's focus ID rather than the field's current focus. The field's OnFocusLost handler never clears that ID, so moving focus to an unregistered widget, such as the GPU scene, can leave the native text client active and route editing operations to an unfocused field.
findings.suggestion: Derive activation from the text field's actual focus state, or clear f.focus when the field loses focus and publish the resulting inactive state. Test moving focus from the field to an unregistered focusable widget.
